about: Town services (#9895). Lines are chosen in order: the first whose `when` tags all hold (wet, dry, night, day, port, town) is used; a line without `when` always holds. Text may use {town}, {host}, {service}. Actions: talk (a reply only), meal (eat once a visit), rest (sleep: until morning by night, or `hours` by day), resupply (top the pack's `item` up to `allotment`, once a visit). Outcome templates describe what an action changed, in real game terms.

inn.summary: A meal, a room, a little company

welcome.text: ‘Come in out of that weather. There’s a place by the fire, and the kettle’s still warm.’
‘Late on the road? Come in, the fire’s banked but it’s warm.’
‘Come in and put your pack down. You’ve time for a cup before the road calls again.’

reply.text: ‘Nothing’s putting out in this. The boats are snug at the quay and their crews are in here, mostly.’
‘A good tide this morning. If you’re heading upriver, the barges will tell you how the water’s running.’
‘The river’s high today. The ferry folk are keeping an eye on it. No harm in waiting here until the rain eases.’
‘The ferry’s been busy since breakfast. If you’re heading upriver, you’ll find company at the landing.’

label.text: I’d like to sit a while

reply.text: ‘You’re welcome to sit a while.’ {host} turns a cup in their hands. ‘Someone will be down soon with the day’s news.’

choices.detail: Bread and a bowl by the hearth

reply.text: {host} brings a bowl and pulls out a chair. ‘Take your time. There’s more bread if you need it.’
‘The room above the porch is yours.’ {host} sets a key on the table. ‘Leave your wet things by the fire.’

choices.detail: Dry out and rest a couple of hours

label.text: Rest by the fire a while

reply.text: ‘Pull that chair closer. Nobody will hurry you.’

provisioner.summary: Food and dry things for the road

welcome.text: ‘Shake that off by the door. There’s food for the road, lamp oil, and a few dry things.’
‘Set your pack on the bench. There’s food for the road and lamp oil.’

reply.text: The provisioner wraps the rations in paper. ‘They’ll keep a few days. Mind the weather.’
A flask is set carefully on the counter. ‘Best keep it upright in your pack.’

outcomes.rest: Slept {hours} h · health {health} · food {food} · damp {wet} · chill {chill}
outcomes.pack-full: Your pack is too full to take more

hint: Prototype rules: talking and browsing cost no time. Resting advances the clock under the usual rules. Meals and supplies are free, once a visit, and supplies top your pack up to a road allotment. There is no money yet.
